pages.title: Custom dictionaries
pages._note: Dictionaries are fetched from filinq's own PHP controller (organisation-gated, term-count-enriched) not a plain OR index endpoint — same rationale as ConsentIndex; type:custom preserves that data path.

pages.title: Custom Dictionary Detail
pages._note: Term management (add/remove/import) + metadata edit for one dictionary, fetched via customDictionaryStore. type:custom preserves the filinq-controller data path.

pages.title: Anonymization
pages._note: Anonymization uses the anonymization store (filinq API) not OpenRegister; type:custom preserves the existing data path.

pages.title: Folder Analysis
pages._note: Folder-level anonymization scan; fetches via folderAnonymizationStore (filinq API); type:custom preserves the existing data path.

pages.title: My Documents
pages._note: Hosts the in-app file viewer (FileViewerPage renders when fileViewerStore.currentFile is set). The anonymisation widget routes here after upload so the user reviews detected entities next to the document contents.

pages.title: Shared links
pages._note: share-document-links 3.3: the documentShare records, reached from the options menu on My documents rather than the main menu. type:custom because Take back goes through filinq's DELETE api/shares/{id}, which also deletes the Nextcloud share and a bundle's archive; the index page type's delete would only remove the record.

pages.title: Batch operations
pages._note: redaction-at-scale REQ-DDRAS-003: OpenRegister lists the anonymizationBatch objects directly, and its cascade decides who sees which: the owner bypass gives a user their own batches, policy-admins and admins see all. Progress and documents per hour are written with every batch write from the batch's own files (BatchProgress). A row opens BatchOperationDetail, which polls the status endpoint and carries cancel, resume and the QA sample.

pages.title: Batch
pages._note: One batch (REQ-DDRAS-003/004/005/007) as a declarative type:detail page: the anonymizationBatch record's own fields render in the details widget. The live part is a bodyWidgets section (BatchOperationDetail) because it polls GET api/anonymization/batch/{id}/status while the batch runs, carries cancel and resume behind their own confirmation dialogs (POST .../cancel, .../resume) and lists the QA-sampled files with their review outcome; its props carry @objectId.

pages.title: Review workbench
pages._note: Per-document anonymisation review: the original beside the anonymised result (DocumentCompare), the findings table as the decision panel, selection to a manual entity, and the reviewed mark the commit gate reads (/api/review/{fileId}). Opened from the file viewer's sidebar, which passes name, path and mime in the query; type:custom because the data comes from the anonymisation store and filinq's review endpoints, not a plain OR index.
